record.original_question: Which compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces admit finite manifold quotients that are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric?

evidence.quote: Question 1.15. Which compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces cover isospectral and non-isometric manifolds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is determined spectrally by the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of its Laplace–Beltrami operator acting on smooth functions. Two closed Riemannian manifolds are called Laplace-isospectral if these spectra coincide, and isometric if there exists a smooth distance-preserving bijection between them.

A compact simply connected Riemannian symmetric space is irreducible if it is not isometric to a Riemannian product of two lower-dimensional symmetric spaces. Such spaces are classified by É. Cartan.

Determine the complete list of compact simply connected irreducible Riemannian symmetric spaces $\widetilde M$ with the following property: there exist two closed Riemannian manifolds $M_1$ and $M_2$, both of which are quotients $\widetilde M/\Gamma_i$ by finite groups $\Gamma_i$ of isometries acting freely on $\widetilde M$, such that $M_1$ and $M_2$ are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2023/2024 survey-style preprint on quotients of compact symmetric spaces. While many particular families (notably compact simple Lie groups with bi-invariant metrics, lens-space-type quotients of spheres, and rank-one cases) are known to admit such isospectral non-isometric quotients, a complete classification across all compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces does not appear to have been established. No source was found resolving the problem in full.
